'''David B. Malament''' (born 21 December 1947) is an American [[philosophy of science|philosopher of science]] specializing in the [[philosophy of physics]].

==Biography==
Malament attended [[Stuyvesant High School]] and received a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] degree in [[mathematics]] in 1968 from [[Columbia University]] and a Ph.D. degree in philosophy in 1975 from [[Rockefeller University]]. After teaching for nearly a quarter-century at the [[University of Chicago]], Malament left to become Distinguished Professor of Logic and Philosophy of Science at the [[University of California, Irvine]], where he is now emeritus.  His book ''Topics in the Foundations of General Relativity and Newtonian Gravitation Theory'' (Chicago, 2012) was awarded the 2014 [[Lakatos Award]].

Malament's work focuses the conceptual foundations of the [[Special theory of relativity|special]] and [[General theory of relativity|general]] [[Theory of Relativity|theories of relativity]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Malament | first1 = D. B. | title = The class of continuous timelike curves determines the topology of spacetime | doi = 10.1063/1.523436 | journal = Journal of Mathematical Physics | volume = 18 | issue = 7 | page = 1399| year = 1977 |bibcode = 1977JMP....18.1399M | url = https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-02391730/file/Ontological%20Math%5D%5BPhysics%20mirror%20between%20Noether%20and%20Planck.pdf }}</ref><ref>D. Malament, 2005. "Classical General Relativity" (gr-qc/0506065, to appear in Handbook of the Philosophy of Physics, eds. J. Butterfield and J. Earman, Elsevier) [https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0506065v2 online]</ref> Regarding whether [[Relativity of simultaneity|simultaneity]] in [[special relativity]], the [[Einstein synchronisation]] is conventional, Malament argues against conventionalism and is regarded by some as having refuted [[Adolf Grünbaum]]'s argument for conventionalism.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Malament | first1 =David  | author-link1 = David Malament | year = 1977 | title = Causal Theories of Time and the Conventionality of Simultaneity | journal = Noûs | volume = 11 | issue = 3 | pages = 293–300 | publisher = Wiley | jstor = 2214766| doi =10.2307/2214766 }}</ref> Grünbaum,<ref>A. Grünbaum. ''David Malament and the Conventionality of Simultaneity: A Reply'', [http://philsci-archive.pitt.edu/archive/00000184/ online]</ref> as well as  [[Sahotra Sarkar]] and [[John Stachel]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Sarkar | first1 = Sahotra | last2 = Stachel | first2 = John | year = 1999 | title = Did Malament Prove the Non-Conventionality of Simultaneity in the Special Theory of Relativity? | journal = Philosophy of Science | volume = 66 | issue = 2 | pages = 208–220 | publisher = The University of Chicago Press | jstor = 188643 | doi=10.1086/392684| s2cid = 120008810 }}</ref> don't agree, whereas [[Robert Rynasiewicz]] sides with Malament.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Rynasiewicz | first1 = Robert | author-link1 = Robert Rynasiewicz | year = 2001 | title = Definition, Convention, and Simultaneity: Malament's Result and Its Alleged Refutation by Sarkar and Stachel | journal = Philosophy of Science (Proceedings of the 2000 Biennial Meeting of the Philosophy of Science Association. Part I: Contributed Papers) | volume = 68 | issue = 3 | pages = S345–S357 | publisher = The University of Chicago Press | jstor = 3080957}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Ben-Yami | first1 = H. | title = Causality and Temporal Order in Special Relativity | doi = 10.1093/bjps/axl019 | journal = The British Journal for the Philosophy of Science | volume = 57 | issue = 3 | pages = 459–479 | year = 2006 }}</ref>

During the [[Vietnam War]] Malament was a [[conscientious objector]] to the draft, spending time in jail for refusing induction into the military.<ref>{{cite book|last=Rabinowitz|first=Victor|title=Unrepentant Leftist: A Lawyer's Memoir|year=1996|publisher=University of Illinois Press|isbn=0-252-02253-X|page=[https://archive.org/details/unrepentantlefti0000rabi/page/310 310]|url=https://archive.org/details/unrepentantlefti0000rabi|url-access=registration|quote=David Malament, Vietnam war.}}</ref>   He was in the same jail as the [[Berrigan Brothers (disambiguation)|Berrigan Brothers]], and bunked with [[Phillip Berrigan]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Malament |first1=David |title=Oral history interview with David Malament, 1984 |url=https://dlc.library.columbia.edu/time_based_media/10.7916/d8-smn9-jt86 |website=Columbia University Libraries |access-date=8 January 2026}}</ref>
He published an article on the subject of selective conscientious objection in an early issue of the journal ''[[Philosophy and Public Affairs]]''.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Malament|first=David B.|title=Selective Conscientious Objection and the 'Gillette' Decision|journal=Philosophy & Public Affairs|date=1972|volume=1|pages=1:363–386}}</ref> 

He received the [[Quantrell Award]].<ref name="Prize">{{cite web|title=Llewellyn John and Harriet Manchester Quantrell Awards for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching|url=https://www.uchicago.edu/who-we-are/global-impact/accolades/llewellyn-john-and-harriet-manchester-quantrell-awards-for-excellence-in-undergraduate-teaching|website=UChicago}}</ref>
